description: The plot illustrates how accuracy (ACC) varies with co-occurrence number for several methods. The x-axis is labeled “Co-occurrence Number” and uses a logarithmic scale, spanning from about 0 up to roughly 3×10³, with major tick labels shown at 10¹, 10², and 10³. The y-axis is labeled “ACC (%)” on a linear scale, ranging from 60 to 85 with regularly spaced tick marks every 5 percentage points. Six lines are shown: the Base method is a black solid line with circular markers, increasing from about 61% at the leftmost point to about 67% at the rightmost point; FT is a blue solid line with downward-triangle markers, rising from about 62% to about 68%; IKE is a red solid line with upward-triangle markers, rising from about 64.5% to about 70%; MEND is a brown solid line with diamond markers, increasing from about 66% to about 74%; MEMIT is a purple solid line with pentagon markers, increasing from about 66.5% to about 72.5%; and a green solid line with square markers (label not readable due to a gray overlay in the legend) increases from about 72% at the leftmost point to about 77.5% at the rightmost point, with intermediate points around 76% and ~77.5%.
